text:
dani.r: First-day CI hiccup  our Buildkite step `trigger-gh-workflow` calls the GitHub Actions dispatch endpoint to start a separate workflow (we use it for gated deploys) and it returns 403. I haven't touched org settings yet. Anyone seen this for new hires?

buildkite-bot: Build #3 failed - step: trigger-gh-workflow (exit code: 1)
```
POST https://api.github.com/repos/redwood/deploy-workflows/actions/workflows/deploy.yml/dispatches -> 403 Forbidden
Error: POST ... dispatches: 403 Forbidden - resource requires authentication or insufficient scope
```

infra-lee: Welcome, Dani! That 403 usually means the token used to hit the Actions API doesn't have the `workflows` or `repo` scope, or the GitHub App doesn't have the "Workflows" permission granted. Which token is the step using? A pipeline secret or the Buildkite app?

dani.r: The step shells out to `gh workflow run` and expects GH_TOKEN to be present in the pipeline. I don't see GH_TOKEN in my pipeline vars. I assumed it would be injected.

ci-oncall-bot: Onboarding tip: do not create a personal PAT. Request a scoped CI bot token from #eng-infra or use the shared `deploy-operator` service account. See pinned onboarding checklist.

sam: Quick check: go to https://github.com/apps/buildkite/installations and confirm the Buildkite App shows "Workflows: Read & write" or that the pipeline's token has `workflows` permission. For `gh workflow run` you need either a PAT with `workflow` scope or an app token that includes Workflows write permission.

dani.r: I checked the app page  Buildkite installed for "Some repos" and I don't see Workflows permission listed. What should I do to unblock?

infra-lee: I can provision a short-lived `ci-bot` token scoped to `repo, workflow`. I'll add it masked to the pipeline as SECRET_CI_BOT and then we can re-run the step. Long term we'll swap to dispatching via the `deploy-operator` service to avoid person-scoped tokens.

sam: Added SECRET_CI_BOT (masked) to the pipeline. Also added a tiny preflight in the pipeline to error with a clear message if GH workflow token is missing.

dani.r: Re-ran the job  dispatch step now returns 204 No Content and the downstream workflow started. Huge relief, thanks!

infra-lee: Follow-ups: (1) eng-infra will add a line in the new-hire CI checklist about requesting `ci-bot` or `deploy-operator` for workflow dispatches. (2) We'll check org-level Buildkite App permissions and request Workflows write if needed.

ci-oncall-bot: Build #3 (re-run) passed - step: trigger-gh-workflow :white_check_mark:

dani.r: Thanks all! Appreciate the quick help and the onboarding notes. I'll PR a doc snippet to the checklist once I'm up to speed.
